endorsements.quote: Third, silent prospective validation should run HF-IA in parallel with real care without influencing clinicians, allowing assessment of alert burden, false positives, workflow fit, and safety signals.
Low-risk tasks such as flagging a missing follow-up appointment or creating patient education from an approved template can be automated with audit logs and clinician override.

Finally, versioning should record the source, date, rationale, approved use, and rollback pathway, consistent with broader principles of responsible machine learning deployment and clinical translation ( 13 , 14 ).
Diagnostic outputs should be compared with HF specialist adjudication supported by final clinical diagnosis, echocardiography, natriuretic peptides, and follow-up data.

It also provides a practical implementation path for health systems: begin with low-risk workflow support, then expand only after module-specific validation, usability testing, monitoring, and governance review.

Future validation will require multicenter, de-identified , expert-adjudicated datasets with HFrEF, HFmrEF, HFpEF, acute decompensation, comorbid kidney disease, older adults, women, and underrepresented populations.
Reporting should also reflect new AI-specific guidance for prediction and decision support models – transparent description of sources, intended use, human oversight, model updating ( 18 ).

Future work should therefore proceed in stages: prototype development, retrospective node testing, longitudinal case replay, silent prospective validation, usability assessment, governance review, and only then controlled clinical evaluation.

unlisted_practices: Block or downgrade AI recommendations when critical input data are missing or not current.
Evaluate LLM decision support at the level of individual decision nodes using expert-adjudicated cases before full longitudinal testing.
Test LLM decision support with longitudinal gold-standard case replay, feeding de-identified data in original order and comparing recommendations with expert-defined best actions.
Assess omission errors, such as missed labs or referral triggers, in failure mode analysis of clinical decision support.
Hold new evidence in quarantine until a governance group approves its promotion into active AI recommendations.
Label AI recommendations by evidence status, distinguishing active guideline-based recommendations from emerging evidence.
Assign AI risk tier dynamically based on patient state, missing information, and consequence of error.
Design LLM clinical decision support as separate modules with distinct data requirements, reference standards, and validation pathways instead of one autonomous agent.
Follow DECIDE-AI, CONSORT-AI or SPIRIT-AI when moving to interventional evaluation of AI decision support.

screen.reason: This is a conceptual framework paper proposing design, evaluation, and risk-tiered governance principles for LLM-enabled clinical decision support in heart failure rather than an empirical study.
